$comment: Pack faction id -> retail side token, the vocabulary SKIRMISH_PLAYER_FACTION
and every other side-comparing retail script member speaks.
EVIDENCE. The retail engine compares `player->getSide() ==
pFactionParm->getString()` (ScriptConditions.cpp,
evaluateSkirmishPlayerIsFaction): an EXACT AsciiString equality against the
PlayerTemplate `Side =` declaration in data/ini/playertemplate.ini. BFME2
(F:\BFME2 ini.big, sha256 eef27ecb...) declares playable sides Men, Elves,
Dwarves, Isengard, Mordor, Wild; RotWK adds Angmar (playable) and Arnor
(campaign-only, no pack faction). The decoded library corpus authors exactly
those six BFME2 tokens in current-generation libraries, plus legacy BFME1
tokens (Gondor, Rohan, ElderRaces, Goblin) that no BFME2 PlayerTemplate
declares - those gates answer false in retail too, so they need (and get)
no mapping here.
CARDINALITY: one pack faction id -> exactly one side token (1:1). BFME2's
Men faction covers Gondor AND Rohan content, but its SIDE is the single
token 'Men'; the legacy 'Gondor'/'Rohan' side tokens belong to BFME1
templates that BFME2 does not ship.
CONSUMPTION. The vertical slice injects this table into gameplay rules
(rules['retail_faction_sides']), which the sim hashes ('rules' is a
state-hash static key), and RetailSliceSim.team_retail_side() resolves a
team's pack faction through it. A faction absent from this table REFUSES
loudly at players.faction - it must never answer as though the side simply
did not match.
MODS: a mod that adds a faction adds its pack faction id here (or ships a
pack that carries its side once the importer bakes sides into pack
documents - the long-term home, which requires a pack rebuild).
